classification.difficultyReason: Applies the familiar opposite-double-root proof and coefficient comparison, then interprets the explicit real nonzero domain to obtain strict coefficient inequalities.

content.prompt: The polynomial $P(x)=x^4+ax^2+b$ has a double root at $x=\beta$, where $\beta$ is a real number and $\beta\ne0$. Show that $x=-\beta$ is also a double root of $P(x)$. Hence show that $a<0$ and $b>0$.

answer.short: $P(-\beta)=P'(-\beta)=0$ and $P''(-\beta)\ne0$, so $-\beta$ is also a double root. Then $a=-2\beta^2<0$ and $b=\beta^4>0$.
answer.worked:
$P$ is even, so $P(-\beta)=P(\beta)=0$.
$$\begin{align*}P'(x)&=4x^3+2ax\\P'(-\beta)&=-P'(\beta)\\&=0\end{align*}$$
Also, $P''(x)=12x^2+2a$ is even. Since $\beta$ is a double root, $P''(\beta)\ne0$, and hence $P''(-\beta)=P''(\beta)\ne0$. Therefore $-\beta$ is also a double root.
Since $\beta\ne0$, the two double roots are distinct. The polynomial is monic and has degree four, so
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-\beta)^2(x+\beta)^2\\&=(x^2-\beta^2)^2\\&=x^4-2\beta^2x^2+\beta^4.\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients gives $a=-2\beta^2$ and $b=\beta^4$. Since $\beta$ is real and $\beta\ne0$, $\beta^2>0$, so $a<0$ and $b>0$.
